title: Pen points in an icon frame land on whole units
goal: Drawing with the pen inside a 24 point icon frame puts points on fractions of a unit unless the canvas grid is on, and even with it on the grid is 4 points apart, so a point cannot land on most whole units. The icon success list promises every point lands on a whole unit by snapping to the grid, the keylines and the shapes already drawn.
notes: Success line icon-grid 2. Code: Sources/PhotonzCore/PenDrawing.swift ~510-513 onGrid returns the raw point when there is no grid; never snaps to keylines or other anchors. CanvasGrid off by default (Sources/PhotonzCore/CanvasGrid.swift:75), 4 point spacing (~38), zoom ladder never finer (levels ~413). Icon frame draws no unit lines (Sources/Photonz/CanvasIconKeylines.swift). Tutorial says 'four point grid' at Sources/PhotonzCore/TutorialGuides.swift:2962, update if the rule changes. Whole-unit check exists as SVGWholeUnits. Done task a-new-frame-can-be-an-icon-size-and-an-icon-is-s says snapping was deliberately left out then. Whether the frame draws visible unit lines belongs to the open grid card (the-grid-s-controls-come-back-to-the-tool-bar-as); this task is the snapping only. Read from code, not run; the runner reproduces first.
acceptance: In a new 24 point icon frame at Next defaults, with no setting changed, a pen click lands on the nearest whole unit, and an exported SVG of a shape drawn that way passes the whole-unit check
A pen point also snaps to a keyline and to an anchor of another shape in the frame when it is near one
Outside icon frames the pen behaves exactly as today
A walk draws a path in a 24 frame and checks every anchor is whole, and runs green at Next defaults

Audit written under queue/audits/ with a close picture of snapped points; anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Reproduced before the fix: new walk pen-lands-on-whole-units-in-an-icon-walk, at Next defaults, failed with 'the copied SVG puts 6 place(s) off whole units: transform=3.3, transform=5.6, d=15.3, d=0.8, d=8.1, d=13.1'.

Review before building: a Photoshop/Illustrator user expects pixel snapping in a pixel-sized artboard with no setup, and Cmd as the no-magnets key (the app's rule). Risk: keylines one unit apart (live area 2, square 3) would steal units if the pull were wide, so the pull is 6 view points capped at one unit; zoomed in, rounding alone decides. Targets off whole units (odd frame centre, a point placed with Cmd) are never offered, which keeps every point whole. The canvas grid is ignored inside icon frames: at 4 points apart it reaches one unit in four.

Built: Sources/PhotonzCore/IconSnap.swift (whole units from the frame corner, keylines while shown, other paths' anchors; PhotonzDocument.iconSnap(at:keylines:)). PenSession.iconSnap wins over grid for points, Shift runs (diagonals stay 45 on whole units) and dragged handles. Canvas: CanvasPen.refreshPenSnapping takes the icon under the FIRST anchor, so a path started on bare canvas behaves exactly as before; the landing ring now shows inside icon frames too. Icon tutorial copy no longer says points stick to grid crossings. Tests: IconSnapTests (27). Full suite green (12189). Walks green: the new one plus icon-stroke-weight, icon-width-row x2, pen-path-thickness, tutorial-draw-it-with-the-pen, tutorial-icon-keylines-already-on, tutorial-start-on-an-icon-frame, copy-an-icon-as-svg, icon-keylines, close-an-open-path, join-two-pen-paths, path-reshape, path-arrives-with-no-edge, copy-leaves-the-canvas-out, pen-on-the-grid.

Follow-ups filed: a-curve-drawn-on-whole-units-exports-on-whole-un (reproduced: a whole-unit curve that bulges past its first point exports translate(13.88 6)); icon-snapping-reaches-what-the-icon-mock-draws (the mock's Snap to row, pointer readout, edge and centre targets, Ctrl vs Cmd, and the picked-shape-corner press clash).
